primary.title: The Speeches of Queen Elizabeth I
primary.author: Elizabeth I of England
primary.rationale: Collection of significant speeches delivered by Elizabeth I throughout her reign, offering direct insight into her political thinking and rhetorical style. These are foundational primary sources for understanding her rule.

primary.title: Letters of Queen Elizabeth I
primary.author: Elizabeth I of England
primary.rationale: A compilation of personal and official correspondence, providing intimate details of her relationships, political negotiations, and decision-making processes. Essential for a nuanced understanding of her reign.

primary.title: A Declaration of the Practices and Treasons Attempted by the Scottish Queen
primary.author: Elizabeth I of England
primary.rationale: A public statement issued by Elizabeth I justifying the execution of Mary, Queen of Scots. This document reveals her political maneuvering and her public persona.

secondary.title: Elizabeth I
secondary.author: David Starkey
secondary.rationale: A comprehensive and highly regarded biography by a leading Tudor historian, offering in-depth analysis of Elizabeth's life, reign, and impact.

secondary.title: The Myth of Elizabeth
secondary.author: Anne Somerset
secondary.rationale: Explores the construction and evolution of Elizabeth I's image and legacy, providing critical analysis of how she has been perceived throughout history.

secondary.title: Elizabeth I and Her Parliaments, 1559-1581
secondary.author: J.E. Neale
secondary.rationale: While slightly before the 1976 cutoff, Neale's work is a foundational scholarly text on Elizabeth's relationship with Parliament and is often cited in later scholarship. A revised edition or subsequent works by scholars building on this might be more recent.

suggestions.notes: The primary source 'Letters of Queen Elizabeth I' might be a compilation published posthumously, but the letters themselves are primary. J.E. Neale's work is included as a highly influential precursor to more recent scholarship, though newer editions or related works would be preferable if available.
